**Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on Surah 99, verses 5–8:**

﴿Because your Lord has inspired it﴾. That is: He commanded it to speak and permitted it to inform of what was done upon it. Ibn 'Abbas and al-Qurazi said: "He inspired it (awha ilayha)."

The figurative sense (majaz) of the verse (see: majaz, figurative usage of language): Allah inspires it. It is said: awha laha, awha ilayha, wahha laha and wahha ilayha, all with the same meaning. His saying, exalted is He: ﴿That day people will come forth in scattered groups﴾. People will return from the place of reckoning after the presentation, ﴿in scattered groups﴾, dispersed. Some will take the right way to Paradise and some the left way to the Fire, as in His saying: "That day they will be divided" [Ar-Rum: 14], and "That day they will be separated" [Ar-Rum: 43].

﴿to be shown their deeds﴾. Ibn 'Abbas said: "To be shown the recompense of their deeds." The meaning is that they return from the place of standing in groups, so that they may take their places in Paradise and in the Fire.

﴿So whoever does an atom's weight of good﴾: the weight of a very small ant, the smallest of ants.

﴿will see it. And whoever does an atom's weight of evil will see it﴾. Ibn 'Abbas said: No believer or disbeliever does good or evil in this world except that Allah shows it to him on the Day of Resurrection. [Narrated by al-Tabari: 30/268. al-Suyuti in al-Durr al-Manthur (8/595) adds its attribution to Ibn al-Mundhir and al-Bayhaqi in al-Ba'th.] As for the believer, he sees his good deeds and his bad deeds, so Allah forgives his bad deeds and rewards him for his good deeds. As for the disbeliever, his good deeds are rejected and he is punished for his bad deeds.

Muhammad ibn Ka'b said concerning this verse, "So whoever does an atom's weight of good will see it": from a disbeliever, who sees his reward in this world in his person, his wealth, his family and his children, until he leaves this world with no good with Allah. "And whoever does an atom's weight of evil will see it": from a believer, who sees his punishment in this world in his person, his wealth, his family and his children, until he leaves this world with no evil with Allah.

Muqatil said: This verse was revealed concerning two men. When the verse "and they give food in spite of their love for it" [al-Insan: 8] was revealed, one of them would have a beggar come to him, and he would consider it too much to give him a date, a morsel, a nut or the like, saying: "This is nothing; we are rewarded only for what we give, and we love it." The other would treat small sins lightly, such as a lie, backbiting, a glance and similar things, saying: "Allah only promised the Fire for the major sins, and there is no sin in this." So Allah, exalted is He, revealed this verse, encouraging them to give even a little good, for it will soon grow, and warning them against small sins, for they too will soon grow. [Mentioned by al-Suyuti in al-Durr al-Manthur (8/594–595), attributed to Ibn Abi Hatim from Sa'id ibn Jubayr.] So a small sin in the eyes of its doer is greater than the mountains on the Day of Resurrection, and all of his good deeds [in his eyes] are less than anything.

Ibn Mas'ud said: "The most decisive verse in the Qur'an is: ﴿So whoever does an atom's weight of good will see it, and whoever does an atom's weight of evil will see it﴾."

The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) used to call it the comprehensive, unique verse when he was asked about the zakat on donkeys. He said: "Nothing was revealed to me concerning it except this comprehensive, unique verse: ﴿So whoever does an atom's weight of good will see it, and whoever does an atom's weight of evil will see it﴾." [Narrated by al-Bukhari in Tafsir, Surat al-Zalzalah, chapter "And whoever does an atom's weight of evil will see it" (8/727), and in Jihad, chapter "The horses for three" (6/63–64). Also by Muslim in Zakat, chapter "The sin of one who withholds zakat," no. (987) (2/682).]

'Umar ibn al-Khattab and 'A'ishah gave in charity a single grape, and they said: "In it are many atoms' weights." [See al-Durr al-Manthur: 8/597.]

Al-Rabi' ibn Khuthaym said: A man passed by al-Hasan while he was reciting this surah. When he reached its end, he said: "Enough for me; the admonition has ended." [Narrated by 'Abd al-Razzaq in Tafsir: 2/388.]

We were informed by Ahmad ibn Ibrahim al-Shuraihi: Abu Ishaq al-Tha'labi informed us: Muhammad ibn al-Qasim informed us: Abu Bakr Muhammad 'Abd Allah narrated to us: al-Hasan ibn Sufyan narrated to us: 'Ali ibn Hujr narrated to us: Yazid ibn Harun narrated to us: al-Yaman ibn al-Mughirah narrated to us: 'Ata' narrated to us, from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Idhا zulzilat al-ard" [Surah 99] equals half the Qur'an; "Qul huwa Allahu ahad" [Surah 112] equals one third of the Qur'an; "Qul ya ayyuha al-kafirun" [Surah 109] equals one quarter of the Qur'an.

[Weak. Narrated by al-Tirmidhi in Fada'il al-Qur'an (8/205–206), who said: "This is a strange hadith, which we know only through the narration of Yaman ibn al-Mughirah." al-Hakim authenticated it (1/566), but al-Dhahabi criticized him, saying: "Rather, the scholars weakened Yaman." Also narrated by al-Bayhaqi in Shu'ab al-Iman (5/452) and Ibn 'Adi in al-Kamil (7/2638). See also: Fayd al-Qadir by al-Munawi (1/367); al-Albani's Da'if al-Hakim, no. (531), p. (76).]

The figurative sense (majaz) of the verse (see: majaz, figurative usage of language): Allah inspires it. It is said: awha laha, awha ilayha, wahha laha and wahha ilayha, all with the same meaning. His saying, exalted is He: ﴿That day people will come forth in scattered groups﴾. People will return from the place of reckoning after the presentation, ﴿in scattered groups﴾, dispersed. Some will take the right way to Paradise and some the left way to the Fire, as in His saying: "That day they will be divided" [Ar-Rum: 14], and "That day they will be separated" [Ar-Rum: 43].

﴿to be shown their deeds﴾. Ibn 'Abbas said: "To be shown the recompense of their deeds." The meaning is that they return from the place of standing in groups, so that they may take their places in Paradise and in the Fire.

﴿So whoever does an atom's weight of good﴾: the weight of a very small ant, the smallest of ants.

﴿will see it. And whoever does an atom's weight of evil will see it﴾. Ibn 'Abbas said: No believer or disbeliever does good or evil in this world except that Allah shows it to him on the Day of Resurrection. [Narrated by al-Tabari: 30/268. al-Suyuti in al-Durr al-Manthur (8/595) adds its attribution to Ibn al-Mundhir and al-Bayhaqi in al-Ba'th.] As for the believer, he sees his good deeds and his bad deeds, so Allah forgives his bad deeds and rewards him for his good deeds. As for the disbeliever, his good deeds are rejected and he is punished for his bad deeds.

Muhammad ibn Ka'b said concerning this verse, "So whoever does an atom's weight of good will see it": from a disbeliever, who sees his reward in this world in his person, his wealth, his family and his children, until he leaves this world with no good with Allah. "And whoever does an atom's weight of evil will see it": from a believer, who sees his punishment in this world in his person, his wealth, his family and his children, until he leaves this world with no evil with Allah.

Muqatil said: This verse was revealed concerning two men. When the verse "and they give food in spite of their love for it" [al-Insan: 8] was revealed, one of them would have a beggar come to him, and he would consider it too much to give him a date, a morsel, a nut or the like, saying: "This is nothing; we are rewarded only for what we give, and we love it." The other would treat small sins lightly, such as a lie, backbiting, a glance and similar things, saying: "Allah only promised the Fire for the major sins, and there is no sin in this." So Allah, exalted is He, revealed this verse, encouraging them to give even a little good, for it will soon grow, and warning them against small sins, for they too will soon grow. [Mentioned by al-Suyuti in al-Durr al-Manthur (8/594–595), attributed to Ibn Abi Hatim from Sa'id ibn Jubayr.] So a small sin in the eyes of its doer is greater than the mountains on the Day of Resurrection, and all of his good deeds [in his eyes] are less than anything.

Ibn Mas'ud said: "The most decisive verse in the Qur'an is: ﴿So whoever does an atom's weight of good will see it, and whoever does an atom's weight of evil will see it﴾."

The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) used to call it the comprehensive, unique verse when he was asked about the zakat on donkeys. He said: "Nothing was revealed to me concerning it except this comprehensive, unique verse: ﴿So whoever does an atom's weight of good will see it, and whoever does an atom's weight of evil will see it﴾." [Narrated by al-Bukhari in Tafsir, Surat al-Zalzalah, chapter "And whoever does an atom's weight of evil will see it" (8/727), and in Jihad, chapter "The horses for three" (6/63–64). Also by Muslim in Zakat, chapter "The sin of one who withholds zakat," no. (987) (2/682).]

'Umar ibn al-Khattab and 'A'ishah gave in charity a single grape, and they said: "In it are many atoms' weights." [See al-Durr al-Manthur: 8/597.]

Al-Rabi' ibn Khuthaym said: A man passed by al-Hasan while he was reciting this surah. When he reached its end, he said: "Enough for me; the admonition has ended." [Narrated by 'Abd al-Razzaq in Tafsir: 2/388.]

We were informed by Ahmad ibn Ibrahim al-Shuraihi: Abu Ishaq al-Tha'labi informed us: Muhammad ibn al-Qasim informed us: Abu Bakr Muhammad 'Abd Allah narrated to us: al-Hasan ibn Sufyan narrated to us: 'Ali ibn Hujr narrated to us: Yazid ibn Harun narrated to us: al-Yaman ibn al-Mughirah narrated to us: 'Ata' narrated to us, from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Idhا zulzilat al-ard" [Surah 99] equals half the Qur'an; "Qul huwa Allahu ahad" [Surah 112] equals one third of the Qur'an; "Qul ya ayyuha al-kafirun" [Surah 109] equals one quarter of the Qur'an.

[Weak. Narrated by al-Tirmidhi in Fada'il al-Qur'an (8/205–206), who said: "This is a strange hadith, which we know only through the narration of Yaman ibn al-Mughirah." al-Hakim authenticated it (1/566), but al-Dhahabi criticized him, saying: "Rather, the scholars weakened Yaman." Also narrated by al-Bayhaqi in Shu'ab al-Iman (5/452) and Ibn 'Adi in al-Kamil (7/2638). See also: Fayd al-Qadir by al-Munawi (1/367); al-Albani's Da'if al-Hakim, no. (531), p. (76).]
